ai.definition: Dynamic Bipedal Balance is a control system designed to enable real-time balance correction in two-legged robots, particularly on uneven terrain.
ai.howItWorks: The system employs Model Predictive Control (MPC) algorithms to continuously adjust the center of mass and joint angles of the robot at millisecond intervals. This allows for smooth navigation and stability even when traversing irregular surfaces.
ai.problemSolved: Ensures stability and safety of two-legged robots in dynamic, unstructured environments such as warehouses or construction sites.
ai.manufacturing: Manufactured using advanced robotics and electronics to integrate high-performance sensors, actuators, and computational hardware.
ai.buildProcess: Involves assembly of components including microcontrollers, MEMS sensors (accelerometers, gyroscopes), motor controllers, and battery packs. The system is then programmed with MPC algorithms for real-time balance control.
ai.costDrivers: High-performance sensor technology, advanced computational resources, and specialized software development are significant cost factors.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to see increased adoption in logistics and manufacturing sectors as demand for automated two-legged robots grows.
ai.regulation: Currently not heavily regulated but may face future standards related to safety and performance in industrial applications.
ai.risks: Technical challenges include ensuring robustness against environmental factors, optimizing energy efficiency, and addressing potential safety hazards.
ai.profitability: Potential for high profitability given the increasing demand for automated solutions in logistics and manufacturing; however, initial costs may limit market entry.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments could focus on enhancing real-time performance, improving battery life, and expanding to new applications such as search and rescue or healthcare.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking processes.

glossary.def: A control strategy that uses a mathematical model of the system to predict future behavior and optimize control inputs in real-time.
The point at which all mass of an object can be considered to be concentrated for the purpose of understanding its motion or balance.

subsystems.name: State estimation
subsystems.role: works out where the body is, how it is tilted and where the feet are touching.

subsystems.name: Terrain and contact model
subsystems.role: predicts where the next foot can land and how much it will grip.

subsystems.name: Centroidal planner (MPC)
subsystems.role: re-plans the centre of mass and foot forces over a short horizon, hundreds of times a second.

subsystems.name: Whole-body controller
subsystems.role: converts the plan into torque commands at every joint.

subsystems.name: Actuators and limbs
subsystems.role: deliver large, fast, back-drivable torque at the ankle, knee and hip.

subsystems.name: Reflex and safety layer
subsystems.role: catches the pushes and trips that the slow planner cannot.

buildSteps.title: Model the body
buildSteps.detail: Measure every link's mass and inertia and write the equations of motion, including contact with the ground, into a physics simulator such as MuJoCo.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the machine
buildSteps.detail: Fit an inertial measurement unit on the pelvis, encoders at each joint and force sensors in the feet, then calibrate them against each other.

buildSteps.title: Build the state estimator
buildSteps.detail: Fuse inertial data with leg kinematics so the robot knows its pelvis velocity and foot positions; handle the sharp impact spikes when a foot lands.

buildSteps.title: Write the balance planner
buildSteps.detail: Approximate the robot as a point mass on an extendable leg, predict its motion 0.5–1 s ahead, and solve a constrained optimisation each control tick for the centre-of-mass acceleration and foot forces.

buildSteps.title: Add the whole-body controller
buildSteps.detail: Turn the plan into joint torques by inverse dynamics or a task-priority quadratic program, respecting torque, joint-limit and self-collision constraints.

buildSteps.title: Grow the reflex layer
buildSteps.detail: Add fast heuristics — capture-point stepping, swing-leg retraction — that act within one or two ticks when the robot is pushed.

buildSteps.title: Train and validate in simulation
buildSteps.detail: Run millions of simulated steps, randomising mass, friction, latency and sensor noise, so the controller survives conditions it was not tuned for.

buildSteps.title: Test in escalating stages
buildSteps.detail: Standing, then push recovery on a harness, then flat-floor walking, then ramps, rubble and stairs, always with an overhead gantry or soft floor as a fallback.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with limits
buildSteps.detail: Derate torque and speed in the field, log every contact event, and keep a remote operator able to halt the robot.

prerequisites.why: balance needs joints that can be commanded in torque and back-driven, not just positioned.
the optimisation and controller must finish in well under one control tick, a few hundred to a few thousand times per second.
without reliable tilt and foot-load data the estimator drifts and the robot falls.

prerequisites.tech: Fast physics simulation and sim-to-real transfer
prerequisites.why: most control policies are learned or tuned in simulation and still suffer from the reality gap.

prerequisites.tech: Energy storage light enough to carry
prerequisites.why: untethered operation for a full shift is still limited by battery mass.

pathway.milestone: humanoids in warehouses doing structured tote and kitting tasks on flat floors
pathway.unlocks: early commercial value where the ground is predictable.

pathway.milestone: reliable balance on gravel, slopes, stairs and after being pushed by a person
pathway.unlocks: construction sites, plant rooms and last-metre delivery.

pathway.milestone: learned policies combined with model-based MPC
pathway.unlocks: recovery from slips and unseen terrain without hand-written rules.

pathway.milestone: fleet-scale reliability and lower unit cost
pathway.unlocks: many robots per site, maintained like other industrial machinery.
